title: A backend validator returning false does not enter an exception fallback
applies_when: A wrapper catches exceptions around a dependency validator and a lead claims that a rejected size, dtype or configuration silently enters a weaker fallback.
lesson: Read the exact dependency version and distinguish its false return from an escaping exception before constructing a regression. SGLang's FlashInfer workspace wrapper directly returns the backend validator result; its dimension-only fallback runs only when that call raises. In pinned FlashInfer 0.7.2, the TRTLLM validator catches metadata ValueError and returns False, including incompatible FP32-Lamport mode. That normal rejection requests reconstruction rather than reaching the wrapper's exception branch. MNNVL has a different byte/strategy capacity contract. Inspect the backend signature adaptation and supported dtype-changing caller as well. An arbitrary raising fake can demonstrate the fallback's local behavior, but cannot establish that a supported backend reaches it or that a wrong kernel runs. Acquire a natural supported exception or contradictory dependency contract before spending GPU time or imposing stricter cache keys.
avoid_when: Do not conclude the wrapper is universally safe: an unsupported keyword, dependency regression, malformed metadata or real backend exception can change reachability. Do not equate exact dtype inequality with insufficient storage for every backend, or reject public-helper defects merely because no internal caller was found. This is static version-bound evidence, not an executed backend, distributed collective, CUDA Graph, model or performance result. Advice retrieval is not measured Scout accuracy or PR conversion.

evidence.note: is_buffer_size_sufficient directly returns the backend result; only escaping exceptions reach dimension-only reuse. Initialization inspects the backend's use_oneshot/strategy signature, records dtype and forwards real input dtype from residual/RMSNorm calls.
Pins flashinfer_python[cu13] to 0.7.2. Read the matching dependency rather than assuming that an old or invented backend lacks its size-check API.
The v0.7.2 commit's TRTLLMAllReduceFusionWorkspace catches the metadata validator's ValueError and returns False. It does not propagate normal insufficiency to the caller's exception handler.
check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata rejects FP32-Lamport incompatibility with ValueError; the unified workspace method catches that exception.
MNNVL implements the strategy-valued size-check API and compares required bytes with buffer_size_bytes. This source contract is not proof that every strategy, version or runtime call succeeds.
